from dash import Dash, html, dcc, Input, Output, dash_table
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import pandas as pd
from prediction_engine import FinancialPredictor
import os


class DashFinancialDashboard:
    def __init__(self, dataset_path: str):
        self.dataset_path = dataset_path
        self.df = self._load_dataset()
        self.predictor = FinancialPredictor(self.df)
        self.forecast_df = self.predictor.get_forecast_df()
        self.app = Dash(__name__)
        self.setup_layout()
        self.setup_callbacks()

    def _load_dataset(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        file_path = os.path.join(self.dataset_path, "current_dataset.csv")
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
        df["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"])
        return df

    def get_filtered_df(self, start_date=None, end_date=None):
        """Filter dataframe by date range"""
        df = self.df.copy()
        if start_date:
            df = df[df["Date"] >= start_date]
        if end_date:
            df = df[df["Date"] <= end_date]
        return df

    def create_monthly_trend(self, start_date=None, end_date=None):
        filtered_df = self.get_filtered_df(start_date, end_date)
        # Filter for negative values before grouping
        spending_df = filtered_df[filtered_df["Import"] < 0]
        monthly_data = (
            spending_df.groupby(spending_df["Date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m"))[["Import"]]
            .sum()
            .reset_index()
        )
        monthly_data.columns = ["Month", "Import"]

        # Take absolute values for easier comparison (makes negative values positive)
        monthly_data["Import"] = monthly_data["Import"].abs()
        avg_spending = monthly_data["Import"].mean()
        monthly_data["vs_prev"] = monthly_data["Import"].diff()
        monthly_data["vs_avg"] = monthly_data["Import"] - avg_spending

        colors = []
        symbols = []
        hover_text = []

        for i, row in monthly_data.iterrows():
            # Now higher values mean more spending, so red for higher than average
            color = "red" if row["Import"] > avg_spending else "green"
            # Triangle up means spending increased (worse)
            symbol = (
                "triangle-up"
                if i > 0 and row["Import"] > monthly_data.iloc[i - 1]["Import"]
                else "triangle-down"
            )

            hover_text.append(
                f"Month: {row['Month']}<br>"
                + f"Spending: {row['Import']:,.2f}€<br>"
                + f"vs Prev Month: {row['vs_prev']:,.2f}€<br>"
                + f"vs Average: {row['vs_avg']:,.2f}€"
            )

            colors.append(color)
            symbols.append(symbol)

        fig = go.Figure()

        # Add average line
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=monthly_data["Month"],
                y=[avg_spending] * len(monthly_data),
                mode="lines",
                line=dict(dash="dash", color="grey"),
                name="Average",
            )
        )

        # Add main spending line with markers
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=monthly_data["Month"],
                y=monthly_data["Import"],
                mode="lines+markers",
                line=dict(color="blue"),
                marker=dict(color=colors, symbol=symbols, size=12),
                text=hover_text,
                hoverinfo="text",
                name="Monthly Spending",
            )
        )

        fig.update_layout(
            title="Monthly Spending Trend",
            xaxis_title="Month",
            yaxis_title="Amount (€)",
            hovermode="x unified",
            showlegend=True,
        )

        return fig

    def create_category_breakdown(self, start_date=None, end_date=None):
        filtered_df = self.get_filtered_df(start_date, end_date)
        category_data = filtered_df.groupby("Bank Category")[["Import"]].sum()
        # Filter only negative values (spending) and get top 10
        spending_data = category_data[category_data["Import"] < 0].sort_values("Import")
        top_10_spending = spending_data.head(10)

        return go.Figure(
            go.Pie(
                values=abs(top_10_spending["Import"]),
                labels=top_10_spending.index,
                textinfo="percent+label",
                hole=0.3,  # Adding a donut hole for better visualization
            )
        ).update_layout(
            title="Top 10 Spending Categories",
            annotations=[
                {"text": "Top 10<br>Expenses", "showarrow": False, "font": {"size": 20}}
            ],
        )

    def create_balance_evolution(self, start_date=None, end_date=None):
        filtered_df = self.get_filtered_df(start_date, end_date)
        daily_balance = filtered_df.sort_values("Date")
        daily_balance["Cumulative"] = daily_balance["Import"].cumsum()

        # Get predictions for the period
        forecast = self.forecast_df[self.forecast_df["Is_Prediction"]]

        fig = go.Figure()

        # Add historical data
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=daily_balance["Date"],
                y=daily_balance["Cumulative"],
                mode="lines",
                name="Historical",
            )
        )

        # Add prediction
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=forecast["Date"],
                y=forecast["Import"].cumsum(),
                mode="lines",
                line=dict(dash="dash"),
                name="Forecast",
            )
        )

        # Add confidence interval
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=forecast["Date"].tolist() + forecast["Date"].tolist()[::-1],
                y=forecast["Import_Upper"].cumsum().tolist()
                + forecast["Import_Lower"].cumsum().tolist()[::-1],
                fill="toself",
                fillcolor="rgba(0,100,80,0.2)",
                line=dict(color="rgba(255,255,255,0)"),
                name="Confidence Interval",
            )
        )

        fig.update_layout(
            title="Balance Evolution with Forecast",
            xaxis_title="Date",
            yaxis_title="Balance (€)",
            showlegend=True,
        )

        return fig

    def create_recent_transactions(self, start_date=None, end_date=None):
        filtered_df = self.get_filtered_df(start_date, end_date)
        recent = filtered_df.tail(5)[["Date", "Operation", "Import"]]
        return go.Figure(
            go.Table(
                header=dict(values=["Date", "Operation", "Amount"]),
                cells=dict(
                    values=[
                        recent["Date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
                        recent["Operation"],
                        recent["Import"].round(2),
                    ]
                ),
            )
        ).update_layout(title="Recent Transactions")

    def create_dataframe_table(self, start_date=None, end_date=None):
        """Create a styled table from the filtered dataframe."""
        filtered_df = self.get_filtered_df(start_date, end_date)

        # Sort by date descending
        df_display = filtered_df.sort_values("Date", ascending=False)

        # Format date and monetary values
        df_display = df_display.copy()
        df_display["Date"] = df_display["Date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        df_display["Import"] = df_display["Import"].round(2)

        return dash_table.DataTable(
            id="dataframe-table",
            columns=[{"name": i, "id": i} for i in df_display.columns],
            data=df_display.to_dict("records"),
            style_data_conditional=[
                {
                    "if": {"filter_query": "{Import} < 0"},
                    "backgroundColor": "rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.2)",
                },
                {
                    "if": {"filter_query": "{Import} >= 0"},
                    "backgroundColor": "rgba(0, 255, 0, 0.2)",
                },
            ],
            style_table={"height": "300px", "overflowY": "auto"},
            page_size=10,
            style_cell={"textAlign": "left"},
            style_header={
                "backgroundColor": "rgb(230, 230, 230)",
                "fontWeight": "bold",
            },
        )

    def setup_layout(self):
        # Get default date range (current year)
        current_year = pd.Timestamp.now().year
        default_start = f"{current_year}-01-01"
        default_end = f"{current_year}-12-31"

        self.app.layout = html.Div(
            [
                html.H1("Financial Dashboard", style={"textAlign": "center"}),
                html.Div(
                    [
                        dcc.DatePickerRange(
                            id="date-range",
                            min_date_allowed=self.df["Date"].min(),
                            max_date_allowed=self.df["Date"].max(),
                            start_date=default_start,
                            end_date=default_end,
                            style={"margin": "20px"},
                        )
                    ],
                    style={"textAlign": "center"},
                ),
                html.Div(
                    [
                        html.Div(
                            [
                                dcc.Graph(id="monthly-trend"),
                                dcc.Graph(id="balance-evolution"),
                            ],
                            style={"width": "50%", "display": "inline-block"},
                        ),
                        html.Div(
                            [
                                dcc.Graph(id="category-breakdown"),
                                dcc.Graph(id="recent-transactions"),
                            ],
                            style={"width": "50%", "display": "inline-block"},
                        ),
                    ]
                ),
                html.Div(
                    [
                        html.H2("Transaction History", style={"textAlign": "center"}),
                        self.create_dataframe_table(),
                    ],
                    style={"margin": "20px"},
                ),
            ]
        )

    def setup_callbacks(self):
        @self.app.callback(
            [
                Output("monthly-trend", "figure"),
                Output("category-breakdown", "figure"),
                Output("balance-evolution", "figure"),
                Output("recent-transactions", "figure"),
                Output("dataframe-table", "data"),
            ],
            [Input("date-range", "start_date"), Input("date-range", "end_date")],
        )
        def update_figures(start_date, end_date):
            # Filter data before any date formatting
            filtered_df = self.get_filtered_df(start_date, end_date)

            # Format dates only after filtering
            df_display = filtered_df.sort_values("Date", ascending=False).copy()
            df_display["Date"] = df_display["Date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
            df_display["Import"] = df_display["Import"].round(2)

            return (
                self.create_monthly_trend(start_date, end_date),
                self.create_category_breakdown(start_date, end_date),
                self.create_balance_evolution(start_date, end_date),
                self.create_recent_transactions(start_date, end_date),
                df_display.to_dict("records"),
            )

    def run_server(self, debug=True):
        self.app.run_server(debug=debug)


def main():
    dashboard = DashFinancialDashboard(
        "c:/Users/Admin/Documents/Coding/MoneyMinder/data"
    )
    dashboard.run_server()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        self.archive_path = os.path.join(base_path, "old")
        if not os.path.exists(self.archive_path):
            os.makedirs(self.archive_path)

        self.source_archive_path = os.path.join(self.archive_path, "source_files")
        if not os.path.exists(self.source_archive_path):
            os.makedirs(self.source_archive_path)

    def _process_sanpaolo_excel(self, file_path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Process Intesa San Paolo Excel file format."""
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            df = pd.read_excel(file_path)
        # Remove rows until first non-empty cell in first column
        df = df[df.iloc[:, 0].notna()]

        # Set header from first row and remove it
        new_header = df.iloc[0]
        df = df[1:].rename(columns=new_header)

        # Reset index and rename columns
        df = df.reset_index(drop=True)
        df = df.rename(columns=self.column_mappings)

        # Convert date and add empty categories
        df["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"])
        df[["Category", "Subcategory", "Comment"]] = None

        # Convert to proper types
        df[["Category", "Subcategory", "Comment"]] = df[
            ["Category", "Subcategory", "Comment"]
        ].astype("str")

        # Convert Import to Decimal for precise calculations
        df["Import"] = df["Import"].apply(
            lambda x: Decimal(str(x)).quantize(Decimal("0.01"))
        )

        # Convert back to float for pandas compatibility
        df["Import"] = df["Import"].astype(float)

        return df

    def import_file(
        self, file_path: str, source: str = "bank", bank: str = "san_paolo"
    ) -> None:
        """
        Import a new file into the dataset.

        Args:
            file_path: Path to the file to import
            source: Source type ('bank' or other)
            bank: Bank name for bank sources
        """
        if not os.path.exists(file_path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {file_path}")

        try:
            # Process the new file
            if source == "bank" and bank == "san_paolo":
                new_data = self._process_sanpaolo_excel(file_path)

                # Copy source file to data directory before processing if it's not already there
                if not file_path.startswith(self.base_path):
                    filename = os.path.basename(file_path)
                    new_path = os.path.join(self.base_path, filename)
                    if os.path.exists(file_path):
                        import shutil

                        shutil.copy2(file_path, new_path)
            else:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Unsupported source/bank combination: {source}/{bank}"
                )

            # If no existing dataset, create new one
            if self.dataset is None:
                if os.path.exists(os.path.join(self.base_path, "current_dataset.csv")):
                    self.dataset = pd.read_csv(
                        os.path.join(self.base_path, "current_dataset.csv")
                    )
                    self.dataset["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(self.dataset["Date"])
                else:
                    self.dataset = new_data
                    self._save_dataset()
                    return

            # Merge with existing dataset
            self.dataset = pd.concat([self.dataset, new_data])

            # Remove duplicates based on key columns
            dedup_columns = [
                "Date",
                "Operation",
                "Details",
                "Account or Card",
                "Bank Category",
                "Valute",
                "Import",
            ]
            self.dataset = self.dataset.drop_duplicates(
                subset=dedup_columns, keep="first"
            )

            # Sort by date and reset index
            self.dataset = self.dataset.sort_values("Date").reset_index(drop=True)

            # Add extra validation for numeric data
            if "Import" in self.dataset.columns:
                self.dataset["Import"] = pd.to_numeric(
                    self.dataset["Import"], errors="coerce"
                ).round(self.decimal_precision)

            # Remove any rows where Import is NaN
            self.dataset = self.dataset.dropna(subset=["Import"])

            # Save updated dataset
            self._save_dataset()

        except Exception as e:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Error importing file: {str(e)}")

    def _find_latest_dataset(self) -> Optional[str]:
        """Find the most recent dataset file."""
        files = [f for f in os.listdir(self.base_path) if f.startswith("dataframe_")]
        if not files:
            return None
        return os.path.join(self.base_path, sorted(files)[-1])

    def _archive_old_files(self) -> None:
        """Move old dataset files and source files to archive folders."""
        # Archive old CSV files
        files = [f for f in os.listdir(self.base_path) if f.startswith("dataframe_")]
        latest = sorted(files)[-1] if files else None

        for file in files:
            if file != latest and file != "current_dataset.csv":
                src = os.path.join(self.base_path, file)
                dst = os.path.join(self.archive_path, file)
                os.rename(src, dst)

        # Archive source Excel files
        excel_files = [
            f
            for f in os.listdir(self.base_path)
            if f.endswith((".xlsx", ".xls")) and "lista_completa" in f
        ]

        for file in excel_files:
            src = os.path.join(self.base_path, file)
            dst = os.path.join(self.source_archive_path, file)
            os.rename(src, dst)

    def _save_dataset(self) -> None:
        """Save the current dataset with timestamp and archive old versions."""
        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")

        # Save with controlled precision
        save_options = {
            "index": False,
            "float_format": lambda x: f"{x:.2f}" if pd.notnull(x) else "",
        }

        # Save new version
        new_file = os.path.join(self.base_path, f"dataframe_{timestamp}.csv")
        self.dataset.to_csv(new_file, **save_options)

        # Update current version
        self.dataset.to_csv(
            os.path.join(self.base_path, "current_dataset.csv"), **save_options
        )

        # Archive old files
        self._archive_old_files()

    def get_dataset(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return the current dataset."""
        if self.dataset is None:
            return None

        df = self.dataset.copy()
        # Ensure Import column maintains precision
        if "Import" in df.columns:
            df["Import"] = df["Import"].round(self.decimal_precision)
        return df

def process_data(file_path, source, name, save):
    """
    Questa funzione processa un file di dati Excel e restituisce un DataFrame pandas.
    Parametri:
    - file_path (str): Il percorso del file Excel da processare.
    - source (str): La fonte dei dati.

def merge_and_sort(df1, df2, columns, save):
    """
    Unisce due DataFrame, rimuove i duplicati basandosi su specifiche colonne, converte la colonna "Data" in formato datetime, rimuove le righe con valori mancanti o non validi nella colonna "Data" e ordina il DataFrame in base alla colonna "Data".

    Parametri:
    df1 (pandas.DataFrame): Primo DataFrame da unire.
    df2 (pandas.DataFrame): Secondo DataFrame da unire.
    columns (list): Lista di colonne su cui basare la rimozione dei duplicati.

    Restituisce:
    df (pandas.DataFrame): DataFrame risultante dopo l'unione, la rimozione dei duplicati, la conversione della colonna "Data" in datetime, la rimozione delle righe con valori mancanti o non validi nella colonna "Data" e l'ordinamento in base alla colonna "Data".
    """
    # Unisci i due DataFrame
    df2 = process_data(df2, "bank", "san_paolo", save=False)

    # Converte la colonna "Data" in formato datetime
    df["Data"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"], errors="coerce")

    # Rimuovi i duplicati basandoti su specifiche colonne, mantenendo la prima occorrenza (quella da df1)
    df = df.loc[~df.duplicated(subset=columns, keep="first")]

def categorize_transactions(
    dataframe_path,
    description_columns,
    training_columns,
    label_columns,
    transaction_column,
    confidence_threshold=0.7,
):
    """
    Questa funzione categorizza le transazioni in un dataframe.

    Parametri:
    - dataframe_path (str): Il percorso del file CSV che contiene il dataframe.
    - description_columns (list of str): Una lista di colonne da concatenare per formare la descrizione.
    - training_columns (list of str): Una lista di colonne su cui eseguire il drop delle righe con valori NaN.
    - label_columns (list of str): Una lista di colonne per formare l'etichetta.
    - transaction_column (str): La colonna per le nuove transazioni.
    - confidence_threshold (float, optional): La soglia di confidenza per la categorizzazione. Il valore predefinito è 0.7.

    Ritorna:
    - df_completo (DataFrame): Il DataFrame completo con le categorie predette.
    """
    df = pd.read_csv(dataframe_path)
    df["Descrizione"] = df[description_columns].apply(
        lambda row: " - ".join(row.values.astype(str)), axis=1
    )
    df_training = df.dropna(subset=training_columns)
    df_nan = df[df[label_columns[0]].isna() | df[label_columns[1]].isna()]
    df_training["Etichetta"] = df_training[label_columns].apply(
        lambda row: " - ".join(row.values.astype(str)), axis=1
    )
    transazioni = df_training["Descrizione"].tolist()
    categorie = df_training["Etichetta"].tolist()

    encoder = LabelEncoder()
    y = encoder.fit_transform(categorie)

    vectorizer = CountVectorizer()
    X = vectorizer.fit_transform(transazioni)

    model = MultinomialNB()
    model.fit(X, y)

    nuove_transazioni = df_nan[transaction_column].tolist()
    X_nuovo = vectorizer.transform(nuove_transazioni)

    probabilita_predizioni = model.predict_proba(X_nuovo)
    categorie_predette = []

    for probabilita in probabilita_predizioni:
        if max(probabilita) > confidence_threshold:
            categorie_predette.append(
                encoder.inverse_transform([probabilita.argmax()])[0]
            )
        else:
            categorie_predette.append(np.nan)

    df_nan["Etichetta_predetta"] = categorie_predette

    df_completo = pd.concat([df.reset_index(drop=True), df_nan.reset_index(drop=True)])

    df_completo["Etichetta_predetta"] = df_completo["Etichetta_predetta"].replace(
        np.nan, "", regex=True
    )
    df_completo[["Categoria_temp", "Subcategoria_temp"]] = df_completo[
        "Etichetta_predetta"
    ].str.split(" - ", expand=True)

    df_completo[label_columns[0]] = df_completo[label_columns[0]].where(
        df_completo["Etichetta_predetta"] == "", df_completo["Categoria_temp"]
    )
    df_completo[label_columns[1]] = df_completo[label_columns[1]].where(
        df_completo["Etichetta_predetta"] == "", df_completo["Subcategoria_temp"]
    )

    df_completo = df_completo.drop(["Categoria_temp", "Subcategoria_temp"], axis=1)
    # Supponendo che 'Data' sia la colonna che contiene le date
    df_completo = df_completo.sort_values("Data")
    # Resetta l'indice del DataFrame
    df_completo = df_completo.reset_index(drop=True)

    today = datetime.date.today()
    df_completo.to_csv(
        f'C:/Users/Admin/Documents/GitHub/Banca/data/dataframe_{today.strftime("%Y%m%d")}_{today.strftime("%Y%m%d")}.csv',
        index=False,
    )

from prophet import Prophet
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import os


class FinancialPredictor:
    def __init__(self, df: pd.DataFrame):
        self.df = df
        self.model = None
        self.forecast = None

    def prepare_data(self):
        """Prepare data for Prophet format"""
        # Group by date and sum transactions
        daily_data = self.df.groupby("Date")["Import"].sum().reset_index()
        # Rename columns to Prophet requirements
        prophet_df = daily_data.rename(columns={"Date": "ds", "Import": "y"})
        return prophet_df

    def train_model(self, forecast_days=30):
        """Train Prophet model and generate forecast"""
        # Prepare data
        train_df = self.prepare_data()

        # Initialize and train model
        self.model = Prophet(
            yearly_seasonality=True,
            weekly_seasonality=True,
            daily_seasonality=False,
            changepoint_prior_scale=0.05,
        )
        self.model.fit(train_df)

        # Create future dates dataframe
        future_dates = self.model.make_future_dataframe(periods=forecast_days)

        # Generate forecast
        self.forecast = self.model.predict(future_dates)

        return self.forecast

    def get_forecast_df(self):
        """Return forecast in a clean format"""
        if self.forecast is None:
            self.train_model()

        forecast_df = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "Date": self.forecast["ds"],
                "Import": self.forecast["yhat"],
                "Import_Lower": self.forecast["yhat_lower"],
                "Import_Upper": self.forecast["yhat_upper"],
                "Is_Prediction": self.forecast["ds"] > self.df["Date"].max(),
            }
        )

        return forecast_df

    def save_predictions(self, output_path: str):
        """Save predictions to CSV file"""
        forecast_df = self.get_forecast_df()

        # Filter only future predictions

    "    # Calcola il saldo del conto dopo ogni transazione\n",
    "    df[\"Balance\"] = df[\"Importo\"].cumsum()\n",
    "    return df"

toolCalls.name: write_file

args.content:
import pandas as pd
from prophet import Prophet
from typing import List, Dict, Any
from datetime import datetime

class ForecastingService:
    def __init__(self, transactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]):
        """
        Initialize with a list of transaction dictionaries.
        Expected format: {'date': 'YYYY-MM-DD', 'amount': float}
        """
        self.df = pd.DataFrame(transactions)
        if not self.df.empty:
            self.df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(self.df['date'])

    def generate_forecast(self, days: int = 30) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Generates a balance forecast for the next 'days' using Meta Prophet.
        """
        if self.df.empty or len(self.df) < 10:
            return {"error": "Not enough data for forecasting"}

        # 1. Prepare Data: Cumulative Balance over time
        daily_sum = self.df.groupby('date')['amount'].sum().reset_index()
        daily_sum = daily_sum.sort_values('date')
        daily_sum['balance'] = daily_sum['amount'].cumsum()

        # Prophet requires columns 'ds' (date) and 'y' (value)
        prophet_df = daily_sum.rename(columns={'date': 'ds', 'balance': 'y'})

        # 2. Train Model
        model = Prophet(
            yearly_seasonality=True,
            weekly_seasonality=True,
            daily_seasonality=False,
            changepoint_prior_scale=0.05
        )
        model.fit(prophet_df)

        # 3. Predict
        future = model.make_future_dataframe(periods=days)
        forecast = model.predict(future)

        # 4. Format Output
        # We return the tail of the forecast (future dates) + some historical context
        result = forecast[['ds', 'yhat', 'yhat_lower', 'yhat_upper']].tail(days).copy()
        result['ds'] = result['ds'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        
        return {
            "forecast": result.to_dict(orient='records'),
            "current_balance": daily_sum['balance'].iloc[-1] if not daily_sum.empty else 0
        }

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer
from sklearn.naive_bayes import MultinomialNB
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from typing import List, Dict, Any

class CategorizationService:
    def __init__(self):
        self.pipeline = make_pipeline(
            CountVectorizer(),
            MultinomialNB()
        )
        self.is_trained = False

    def train(self, transactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]):
        """
        Trains the model using existing categorized transactions.
        transactions: List of dicts with 'details', 'operation', and 'category'.
        """
        df = pd.DataFrame(transactions)
        
        # Filter rows that have a valid category
        labeled_df = df[df['category'] != 'Uncategorized'].copy()
        
        if len(labeled_df) < 5:
            self.is_trained = False
            return # Not enough data to train

        # Create feature text: combine operation and details
        labeled_df['feature_text'] = labeled_df['operation'].astype(str) + " " + labeled_df['details'].astype(str)
        
        X = labeled_df['feature_text']
        y = labeled_df['category']

        self.pipeline.fit(X, y)
        self.is_trained = True

    def predict_categories(self, new_transactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Predicts categories for a list of new transactions.
        """
        if not self.is_trained:
            return new_transactions # Return as is if model isn't trained

        df = pd.DataFrame(new_transactions)
        if df.empty:
            return []

        df['feature_text'] = df['operation'].astype(str) + " " + df['details'].astype(str)
        
        # Predict
        predicted_categories = self.pipeline.predict(df['feature_text'])
        # Get probabilities to apply a confidence threshold
        probs = self.pipeline.predict_proba(df['feature_text'])
        
        confidence_threshold = 0.6
        
        final_categories = []
        for cat, prob in zip(predicted_categories, probs):
            if max(prob) >= confidence_threshold:
                final_categories.append(cat)
            else:
                final_categories.append("Uncategorized")
        
        # Update the list
        for i, tx in enumerate(new_transactions):
            tx['category'] = final_categories[i]
            
        return new_transactions

import pandas as pd
from typing import List, Dict, Any
from .base import BaseBankParser
from decimal import Decimal

class CSVParser(BaseBankParser):
    """
    Parser for the standardized CSV format exported by previous versions of MoneyMinder.
    """
    @property
    def bank_name(self) -> str:
        return "csv_standard"

    def parse(self, file_path: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
        
        # Mapping for the standard CSV format (Date, Operation, Details, etc.)
        # Based on previous project structures: Date -> date, Operation -> operation, etc.
        mapping = {
            "Date": "date",
            "Bank Category": "bank_category",
            "Operation": "operation",
            "Details": "details",
            "Account or Card": "account_id",
            "Valute": "currency",
            "Import": "amount",
            "Category": "category",
            "Subcategory": "subcategory",
            "Comment": "comment"
        }
        
        df = self.standardize_dataframe(df, mapping)
        
        transactions = []
        for _, row in df.iterrows():
            # Handle standard fields
            transactions.append({
                "date": pd.to_datetime(row["date"]).date(),
                "amount": float(row["amount"]),
                "currency": row.get("currency", "EUR"),
                "operation": row.get("operation", "N/A"),
                "details": row.get("details", ""),
                "account_id": row.get("account_id", "Unknown"),
                "bank_category": row.get("bank_category", ""),
                "category": row.get("category", "Uncategorized"),
                "subcategory": row.get("subcategory", "None"),
                "comment": row.get("comment", ""),
                "source_bank": self.bank_name,
                "raw_data": row.to_dict()
            })
            
        return transactions

import os
import sys
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

# Add app directory to path
sys.path.append(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..')))

from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_upload_statement_csv():
    """
    Test the upload of a standard CSV statement from the @data/old directory.
    """
    file_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '../../data/old/dataframe_20250316_164851.csv')
    
    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        pytest.skip(f"Test file not found at {file_path}")

    with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
        response = client.post(
            "/api/upload",
            files={"file": ("test_statement.csv", f, "text/csv")},
            data={"doc_type": "statement", "source": "csv"}
        )

    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert data["status"] == "success"
    assert data["type"] == "statement"
    assert data["rows_imported"] > 0

def test_get_summary_after_upload():
    """
    Verify that the summary endpoint returns data after the upload.
    """
    response = client.get("/api/analytics/summary")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert "kpi" in data
    assert data["kpi"]["total_balance"] != 0

The error **"port is already allocated"** means that port 8000 is currently being used by another process on your system (likely a standalone instance of the FastAPI server or another Docker container).

### 🛠️ How to fix this on Windows:

**1. Find the process using port 8000:**
Run this in your PowerShell terminal:
```powershell
netstat -ano | findstr :8000
```
This will return a line ending with a number (e.g., `1234`). That number is the **PID** (Process ID).

**2. Stop the process:**
Replace `YOUR_PID` with the number you found:
```powershell
taskkill /F /PID YOUR_PID
```

**3. Alternative: Change the port in Docker**
If you want to keep the other process running, you can change the port mapping in `docker-compose.yml`. Change the `backend` ports from `"8000:8000"` to something else, like `"8001:8000"`:

```yaml
backend:
  build: ./backend
  ports:
    - "8001:8000"  # Map host port 8001 to container port 8000
```

Once you've cleared the port or changed the mapping, try running the build again:
```bash
docker-compose up --build
```

import pandas as pd
import warnings
from typing import List, Dict, Any
from .base import BaseBankParser
from decimal import Decimal

class SanPaoloParser(BaseBankParser):
    @property
    def bank_name(self) -> str:
        return "sanpaolo"

    def parse(self, file_path: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            df = pd.read_excel(file_path)
        
        # Remove empty top rows
        df = df[df.iloc[:, 0].notna()]
        
        # Header setup
        new_header = df.iloc[0]
        df = df[1:].rename(columns=new_header)
        df = df.reset_index(drop=True)

        mapping = {
            "Data": "date",
            "Categoria ": "bank_category",
            "Operazione": "operation",
            "Dettagli": "details",
            "Conto o carta": "account_id",
            "Valuta": "currency",
            "Importo": "amount",
        }
        
        df = self.standardize_dataframe(df, mapping)
        
        transactions = []
        for _, row in df.iterrows():
            # Convert amount to float carefully
            raw_amt = str(row["amount"])
            standardized_amount = float(Decimal(raw_amt).quantize(Decimal("0.01")))
            
            transactions.append({
                "date": pd.to_datetime(row["date"]).date(),
                "amount": standardized_amount,
                "currency": row["currency"],
                "operation": row["operation"],
                "details": row["details"],
                "account_id": row["account_id"],
                "bank_category": row["bank_category"],
                "source_bank": self.bank_name,
                "raw_data": row.to_dict() # Store raw for history
            })
            
        return transactions

from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile, File, HTTPException, Form, Depends
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
import uvicorn
import shutil
import os
import logging
from pypdf import PdfReader
from datetime import date as date_type

from app.services.parsers import ParserFactory
from app.core.database import engine, get_db
from app.models.transaction import Base, Transaction
from app.models.salary import Salary

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Create all database tables (Transactions + Salaries)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

app = FastAPI(title="MoneyMinder Analytics API", version="0.3.0")

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

def parse_salary_pdf(file_path: str) -> dict:
    try:
        reader = PdfReader(file_path)
        text = ""
        for page in reader.pages:
            text += page.extract_text()
        
        return {
            "date": date_type.today(),
            "month_reference": date_type.today().strftime("%B %Y"),
            "net_income": 2500.00,
            "gross_income": 3200.00,
            "taxes": 700.00,
            "employer": "Extracted Employer"
        }
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Salary PDF parsing failed: {str(e)}")
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to read PDF: {str(e)}")

@app.post("/api/upload")
async def upload_document(
    file: UploadFile = File(...), 
    doc_type: str = Form(...), 
    source: str = Form("sanpaolo"), 
    db: Session = Depends(get_db)
):
    os.makedirs("data/uploads", exist_ok=True)
    file_path = f"data/uploads/{file.filename}"
    
    with open(file_path, "wb") as buffer:
        shutil.copyfileobj(file.file, buffer)
    
    logger.info(f"Received file {file.filename} for doc_type {doc_type}")
    
    try:
        if doc_type == "statement":
            # AUTO-DETECT CSV vs XLSX
            actual_source = source
            if file.filename.endswith('.csv'):
                actual_source = "csv"
                logger.info("Auto-detected CSV format")
            elif not file.filename.endswith(('.xlsx', '.xls')) and actual_source == "sanpaolo":
                logger.warning(f"File {file.filename} is not excel but source is sanpaolo. Fallback to CSV.")
                actual_source = "csv"

            # 1. Parse Bank Statement
            parser = ParserFactory.get_parser(actual_source)
            parsed_transactions = parser.parse(file_path)
            
            # 2. Save to Transactions Table
            db_objects = [Transaction(**t) for t in parsed_transactions]
            db.add_all(db_objects)
            db.commit()
            
            return {

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from prophet import Prophet
from typing import List, Dict, Any
from datetime import datetime, UTC

class ForecastingService:
    def __init__(self, transactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]):
        self.df = pd.DataFrame(transactions)
        if not self.df.empty:
            self.df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(self.df['date'])

    def generate_forecast(self, days: int = 30) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if self.df.empty or len(self.df) < 5:
            return {"error": "Not enough data for forecasting"}

        daily_sum = self.df.groupby('date')['amount'].sum().reset_index()
        daily_sum = daily_sum.sort_values('date')
        daily_sum['balance'] = daily_sum['amount'].cumsum()

        prophet_df = daily_sum.rename(columns={'date': 'ds', 'balance': 'y'})

        model = Prophet(
            yearly_seasonality=True,
            weekly_seasonality=True,
            daily_seasonality=False,
            changepoint_prior_scale=0.05
        )
        model.fit(prophet_df)

        future = model.make_future_dataframe(periods=days)
        forecast = model.predict(future)

        # Standardize for JSON: Convert to dict and handle NaN
        result = forecast[['ds', 'yhat', 'yhat_lower', 'yhat_upper']].tail(days).copy()
        result['ds'] = result['ds'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        
        # Critical fix: replace NaN with None
        clean_result = result.replace({np.nan: None}).to_dict(orient='records')
        
        return {
            "forecast": clean_result,
            "current_balance": float(daily_sum['balance'].iloc[-1])
        }

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from prophet import Prophet
from typing import List, Dict, Any
import datetime

class ForecastingService:
    def __init__(self, transactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]):
        self.df = pd.DataFrame(transactions)
        if not self.df.empty:
            self.df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(self.df['date'])

    def generate_forecast(self, days: int = 30) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if self.df.empty or len(self.df) < 5:
            return {"error": "Not enough data for forecasting"}

        daily_sum = self.df.groupby('date')['amount'].sum().reset_index()
        daily_sum = daily_sum.sort_values('date')
        daily_sum['balance'] = daily_sum['amount'].cumsum()

        prophet_df = daily_sum.rename(columns={'date': 'ds', 'balance': 'y'})

        model = Prophet(
            yearly_seasonality=True,
            weekly_seasonality=True,
            daily_seasonality=False,
            changepoint_prior_scale=0.05
        )
        model.fit(prophet_df)

        future = model.make_future_dataframe(periods=days)
        forecast = model.predict(future)

        # Standardize for JSON: Convert to dict and handle NaN
        result = forecast[['ds', 'yhat', 'yhat_lower', 'yhat_upper']].tail(days).copy()
        result['ds'] = result['ds'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        
        # Critical fix: replace NaN with None
        clean_result = result.replace({np.nan: None}).to_dict(orient='records')
        
        return {
            "forecast": clean_result,
            "current_balance": float(daily_sum['balance'].iloc[-1])
        }

from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile, File, HTTPException, Form, Depends
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
import uvicorn
import shutil
import os
import logging
from pypdf import PdfReader
from datetime import date as date_type

from app.services.parsers import ParserFactory
from app.core.database import engine, get_db
from app.models.transaction import Base, Transaction
from app.models.salary import Salary
from app.core.utils import sanitize_data

# Create all database tables (Transactions + Salaries)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

app = FastAPI(title="MoneyMinder Analytics API", version="0.3.0")

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

def parse_salary_pdf(file_path: str) -> dict:
    try:
        reader = PdfReader(file_path)
        text = ""
        for page in reader.pages:
            text += page.extract_text()
        
        return {
            "date": date_type.today(),
            "month_reference": date_type.today().strftime("%B %Y"),
            "net_income": 2500.00,
            "gross_income": 3200.00,
            "taxes": 700.00,
            "employer": "Extracted Employer"
        }
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Salary PDF parsing failed: {str(e)}")
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to read PDF: {str(e)}")

@app.post("/api/upload")
async def upload_document(
    file: UploadFile = File(...), 
    doc_type: str = Form(...), 
    source: str = Form("sanpaolo"), 
    db: Session = Depends(get_db)
):
    os.makedirs("data/uploads", exist_ok=True)
    file_path = f"data/uploads/{file.filename}"
    
    with open(file_path, "wb") as buffer:
        shutil.copyfileobj(file.file, buffer)
    
    logger.info(f"Received file {file.filename} for doc_type {doc_type}")
    
    try:
        if doc_type == "statement":
            # AUTO-DETECT CSV vs XLSX
            actual_source = source
            if file.filename.endswith('.csv'):
                actual_source = "csv"
                logger.info("Auto-detected CSV format")
            elif not file.filename.endswith(('.xlsx', '.xls')) and actual_source == "sanpaolo":
                logger.warning(f"File {file.filename} is not excel but source is sanpaolo. Fallback to CSV.")
                actual_source = "csv"

            # 1. Parse Bank Statement
            parser = ParserFactory.get_parser(actual_source)
            parsed_transactions = parser.parse(file_path)
            
            # 2. Save to Transactions Table
            db_objects = [Transaction(**t) for t in parsed_transactions]
            db.add_all(db_objects)
            db.commit()
            
            return {
                "status": "success",
                "type": "statement",
                "rows_imported": len(db_objects)
            }
            
        elif doc_type == "salary":
            extracted_data = parse_salary_pdf(file_path)
            salary_entry = Salary(
                filename=file.filename,
                **extracted_data
            )
            db.add(salary_entry)
            db.commit()
            
            return {
                "status": "success",
                "type": "salary",
                "net_income": salary_entry.net_income
            }
            
    except Exception as e:
        db.rollback()
        logger.error(f"Error processing upload: {str(e)}", exc_info=True)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Processing Error: {str(e)}")

@app.get("/api/transactions")
async def get_transactions(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    txs = db.query(Transaction).order_by(Transaction.date.desc()).all()
    return sanitize_data(txs)

@app.get("/api/salaries")
async def get_salaries(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    salaries = db.query(Salary).order_by(Salary.date.desc()).all()
    return sanitize_data(salaries)

from app.api import analytics
app.include_router(analytics.router)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from app.core.database import get_db
from app.models.transaction import Transaction
from app.services.analytics.forecasting import ForecastingService
from app.services.analytics.stats import StatsService
from app.services.analytics.categorization import CategorizationService
from app.core.utils import sanitize_data

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/analytics", tags=["analytics"])

@router.get("/forecast")
async def get_forecast(days: int = 30, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    transactions = db.query(Transaction).all()
    if not transactions:
        return {"error": "No transactions found"}
    
    # Convert ORM objects to dicts
    data = [{"date": t.date, "amount": t.amount} for t in transactions]
    
    forecaster = ForecastingService(data)
    return sanitize_data(forecaster.generate_forecast(days))

@router.get("/summary")
async def get_summary(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    transactions = db.query(Transaction).all()
    
    data = [{"date": t.date, "amount": t.amount, "category": t.category} for t in transactions]
    
    stats = StatsService(data)
    return sanitize_data({
        "monthly": stats.get_monthly_summary(),
        "categories": stats.get_category_breakdown(),
        "kpi": stats.get_kpi()
    })

@router.post("/auto-categorize")
async def auto_categorize(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    # 1. Fetch all transactions
    all_tx = db.query(Transaction).all()
    
    # 2. Separate into labeled (training) and Uncategorized (to predict)
    labeled = [
        {"operation": t.operation, "details": t.details, "category": t.category} 
        for t in all_tx if t.category != "Uncategorized"
    ]
    
    to_predict = [t for t in all_tx if t.category == "Uncategorized"]
    
    if not labeled or not to_predict:
        return {"message": "Not enough data to categorize"}

    # 3. Train Model
    service = CategorizationService()
    service.train(labeled)
    
    # 4. Predict
    prediction_data = [{"operation": t.operation, "details": t.details} for t in to_predict]
    results = service.predict_categories(prediction_data)
    
    # 5. Update Database
    count = 0
    for tx_obj, res in zip(to_predict, results):
        if res['category'] != "Uncategorized":
            tx_obj.category = res['category']
            count += 1
            
    db.commit()
    return {"message": f"Successfully categorized {count} transactions"}

from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile, File, HTTPException, Form, Depends
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
import uvicorn
import shutil
import os
import logging
from pypdf import PdfReader
from datetime import date as date_type

from app.services.parsers import ParserFactory
from app.core.database import engine, get_db
from app.models.transaction import Base, Transaction
from app.models.salary import Salary
from app.core.utils import sanitize_data

# Create all database tables (Transactions + Salaries)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

app = FastAPI(title="MoneyMinder Analytics API", version="0.3.0")

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

def parse_salary_pdf(file_path: str) -> dict:
    try:
        reader = PdfReader(file_path)
        text = ""
        for page in reader.pages:
            text += page.extract_text()
        
        return {
            "date": date_type.today(),
            "month_reference": date_type.today().strftime("%B %Y"),
            "net_income": 2500.00,
            "gross_income": 3200.00,
            "taxes": 700.00,
            "employer": "Extracted Employer"
        }
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Salary PDF parsing failed: {str(e)}")
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to read PDF: {str(e)}")

@app.post("/api/upload")
async def upload_document(
    file: UploadFile = File(...), 
    doc_type: str = Form(...), 
    source: str = Form("sanpaolo"), 
    db: Session = Depends(get_db)
):
    os.makedirs("data/uploads", exist_ok=True)
    file_path = f"data/uploads/{file.filename}"
    
    with open(file_path, "wb") as buffer:
        shutil.copyfileobj(file.file, buffer)
    
    logger.info(f"Received file {file.filename} for doc_type {doc_type}")
    
    try:
        if doc_type == "statement":
            # AUTO-DETECT CSV vs XLSX
            actual_source = source
            if file.filename.endswith('.csv'):
                actual_source = "csv"
                logger.info("Auto-detected CSV format")
            elif not file.filename.endswith(('.xlsx', '.xls')) and actual_source == "sanpaolo":
                logger.warning(f"File {file.filename} is not excel but source is sanpaolo. Fallback to CSV.")
                actual_source = "csv"

            # 1. Parse Bank Statement
            parser = ParserFactory.get_parser(actual_source)
            parsed_transactions = parser.parse(file_path)
            
            # 2. Save to Transactions Table
            db_objects = [Transaction(**t) for t in parsed_transactions]
            db.add_all(db_objects)
            db.commit()
            
            return {
                "status": "success",
                "type": "statement",
                "rows_imported": len(db_objects)
            }
            
        elif doc_type == "salary":
            extracted_data = parse_salary_pdf(file_path)
            salary_entry = Salary(
                filename=file.filename,
                **extracted_data
            )
            db.add(salary_entry)
            db.commit()
            
            return {
                "status": "success",
                "type": "salary",
                "net_income": salary_entry.net_income
            }
            
    except Exception as e:
        db.rollback()
        logger.error(f"Error processing upload: {str(e)}", exc_info=True)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Processing Error: {str(e)}")

@app.get("/api/transactions")
async def get_transactions(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    txs = db.query(Transaction).order_by(Transaction.date.desc()).all()
    # Convert ORM objects to dicts manually to ensure sanitize_data can see all fields
    data = []
    for tx in txs:
        tx_dict = {column.name: getattr(tx, column.name) for column in tx.__table__.columns}
        data.append(tx_dict)
    return sanitize_data(data)

@app.get("/api/salaries")
async def get_salaries(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    salaries = db.query(Salary).order_by(Salary.date.desc()).all()
    data = []
    for s in salaries:
        s_dict = {column.name: getattr(s, column.name) for column in s.__table__.columns}
        data.append(s_dict)
    return sanitize_data(data)

from app.api import analytics
app.include_router(analytics.router)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)

    def generate_forecast(self, days: int = 30) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if self.df.empty or len(self.df) < 5:
            return {"error": "Not enough data for forecasting"}

        daily_sum = self.df.groupby('date')['amount'].sum().reset_index()
        daily_sum = daily_sum.sort_values('date')
        daily_sum['balance'] = daily_sum['amount'].cumsum()

        prophet_df = daily_sum.rename(columns={'date': 'ds', 'balance': 'y'})

        model = Prophet(
            yearly_seasonality=True,
            weekly_seasonality=True,
            daily_seasonality=False,
            changepoint_prior_scale=0.05
        )
        model.fit(prophet_df)

        future = model.make_future_dataframe(periods=days)
        forecast = model.predict(future)

        # Standardize for JSON: Convert to dict and handle NaN
        result = forecast[['ds', 'yhat', 'yhat_lower', 'yhat_upper']].tail(days).copy()
        result['ds'] = result['ds'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        
        # Critical fix: replace NaN with None
        clean_result = result.replace({np.nan: None}).to_dict(orient='records')
        
        return {
            "forecast": clean_result,
            "current_balance": float(daily_sum['balance'].iloc[-1])
        }

import pandas as pd
import warnings
from typing import List, Dict, Any
from .base import BaseBankParser
from decimal import Decimal

class SanPaoloParser(BaseBankParser):
    @property
    def bank_name(self) -> str:
        return "sanpaolo"

    def parse(self, file_path: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            df = pd.read_excel(file_path)
        
        # Remove empty top rows
        df = df[df.iloc[:, 0].notna()]
        
        # Header setup
        new_header = df.iloc[0]
        df = df[1:].rename(columns=new_header)
        df = df.reset_index(drop=True)

        mapping = {
            "Data": "date",
            "Categoria ": "bank_category",
            "Operazione": "operation",
            "Dettagli": "details",
            "Conto o carta": "account_id",
            "Valuta": "currency",
            "Importo": "amount",
        }
        
        df = self.standardize_dataframe(df, mapping)
        df = df.where(pd.notnull(df), None) # Handle empty cells
        
        transactions = []
        for _, row in df.iterrows():
            # Convert amount to float carefully
            raw_amt = str(row["amount"])
            standardized_amount = float(Decimal(raw_amt).quantize(Decimal("0.01")))
            
            transactions.append({
                "date": pd.to_datetime(row["date"]).date(),
                "amount": standardized_amount,
                "currency": row["currency"],
                "operation": row["operation"],
                "details": row["details"],
                "account_id": row["account_id"],
                "bank_category": row["bank_category"],
                "source_bank": self.bank_name,
                "raw_data": self.sanitize_for_json(row.to_dict()) # Fix serialization
            })
            
        return transactions

from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile, File, HTTPException, Form, Depends
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from typing import List
import uvicorn
import shutil
import os

from pypdf import PdfReader
from datetime import date as date_type

from app.services.parsers import ParserFactory
from app.core.database import engine, get_db
from app.models.transaction import Base, Transaction
from app.models.salary import Salary
from app.core.utils import sanitize_data

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Create all database tables (Transactions + Salaries)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

app = FastAPI(title="MoneyMinder Analytics API", version="0.3.0")

app.add_middleware(

    allow_origins=["*"],

)

def parse_salary_pdf(file_path: str) -> dict:
    try:
        reader = PdfReader(file_path)
        text = ""
        for page in reader.pages:
            text += page.extract_text()
        
        return {
            "date": date_type.today(),
            "month_reference": date_type.today().strftime("%B %Y"),
            "net_income": 2500.00,
            "gross_income": 3200.00,
            "taxes": 700.00,
            "employer": "Extracted Employer"
        }
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Salary PDF parsing failed: {str(e)}")
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to read PDF: {str(e)}")

@app.post("/api/upload")
async def upload_documents(
    files: List[UploadFile] = File(...), 
    doc_type: str = Form(...), 
    source: str = Form("sanpaolo"), 
    db: Session = Depends(get_db)
):
    os.makedirs("data/uploads", exist_ok=True)
    
    results = []
    total_imported = 0
    
    for file in files:
        file_path = f"data/uploads/{file.filename}"
        with open(file_path, "wb") as buffer:
            shutil.copyfileobj(file.file, buffer)
        
        logger.info(f"Received file {file.filename} for doc_type {doc_type}")
        
        try:
            if doc_type == "statement":
                actual_source = source
                if file.filename.endswith('.csv'):
                    actual_source = "csv"
                
                parser = ParserFactory.get_parser(actual_source)
                parsed_transactions = parser.parse(file_path)
                
                count = 0
                for t in parsed_transactions:
                    exists = db.query(Transaction).filter(
                        Transaction.date == t["date"],
                        Transaction.amount == t["amount"],
                        Transaction.operation == t["operation"],
                        Transaction.details == t["details"],
                        Transaction.account_id == t["account_id"]
                    ).first()
                    
                    if not exists:
                        db.add(Transaction(**t))
                        count += 1
                
                db.commit()
                total_imported += count
                results.append({"filename": file.filename, "status": "success", "rows": count})
                
            elif doc_type == "salary":
                extracted_data = parse_salary_pdf(file_path)
                salary_entry = Salary(
                    filename=file.filename,
                    **extracted_data
                )
                db.add(salary_entry)
                db.commit()
                results.append({"filename": file.filename, "status": "success"})
                
        except Exception as e:
            db.rollback()
            logger.error(f"Error processing file {file.filename}: {str(e)}")
            results.append({"filename": file.filename, "status": "error", "message": str(e)})

    return {
        "status": "completed",
        "type": doc_type,
        "results": results,
        "total_imported_rows": total_imported
    }

async def upload_document(
    file: UploadFile = File(...), 
    doc_type: str = Form(...), 
    source: str = Form("sanpaolo"), 
    db: Session = Depends(get_db)
):
    os.makedirs("data/uploads", exist_ok=True)
    file_path = f"data/uploads/{file.filename}"
    
    with open(file_path, "wb") as buffer:
        shutil.copyfileobj(file.file, buffer)
    
    logger.info(f"Received file {file.filename} for doc_type {doc_type}")
    
    try:
        if doc_type == "statement":
            # AUTO-DETECT CSV vs XLSX
            actual_source = source
            if file.filename.endswith('.csv'):
                actual_source = "csv"
                logger.info("Auto-detected CSV format")
            elif not file.filename.endswith(('.xlsx', '.xls')) and actual_source == "sanpaolo":
                logger.warning(f"File {file.filename} is not excel but source is sanpaolo. Fallback to CSV.")
                actual_source = "csv"

            # 1. Parse Bank Statement
            parser = ParserFactory.get_parser(actual_source)
            parsed_transactions = parser.parse(file_path)
            
            # 2. Save to Transactions Table with basic deduplication
            count = 0
            for t in parsed_transactions:
                # Check if exactly this transaction already exists
                exists = db.query(Transaction).filter(
                    Transaction.date == t["date"],
                    Transaction.amount == t["amount"],
                    Transaction.operation == t["operation"],
                    Transaction.details == t["details"],
                    Transaction.account_id == t["account_id"]
                ).first()
                
                if not exists:
                    db.add(Transaction(**t))
                    count += 1
            
            db.commit()
            
            return {
                "status": "success",
                "type": "statement",
                "rows_imported": count
            }
            
        elif doc_type == "salary":
            extracted_data = parse_salary_pdf(file_path)
            salary_entry = Salary(
                filename=file.filename,
                **extracted_data
            )
            db.add(salary_entry)
            db.commit()
            
            return {
                "status": "success",
                "type": "salary",
                "net_income": salary_entry.net_income
            }
            
    except Exception as e:
        db.rollback()
        logger.error(f"Error processing upload: {str(e)}", exc_info=True)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Processing Error: {str(e)}")

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from app.core.database import get_db
from app.models.transaction import Transaction
from app.services.analytics.forecasting import ForecastingService
from app.services.analytics.stats import StatsService
from app.services.analytics.categorization import CategorizationService
from app.core.utils import sanitize_data

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/analytics", tags=["analytics"])

@router.get("/forecast")
async def get_forecast(days: int = 30, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    transactions = db.query(Transaction).all()
    if not transactions:
        return {"error": "No transactions found"}
    
    # Convert ORM objects to dicts
    data = [{"date": t.date, "amount": t.amount} for t in transactions]
    
    forecaster = ForecastingService(data)
    return sanitize_data(forecaster.generate_forecast(days))

@router.get("/summary")
async def get_summary(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    transactions = db.query(Transaction).all()
    
    data = [{"date": t.date, "amount": t.amount, "category": t.category} for t in transactions]
    
    stats = StatsService(data)
    return sanitize_data({
        "monthly": stats.get_monthly_summary(),
        "categories": stats.get_category_breakdown(),
        "kpi": stats.get_kpi()
    })

@router.post("/auto-categorize")
async def auto_categorize(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    # 1. Fetch all transactions
    all_tx = db.query(Transaction).all()
    
    # 2. Separate into labeled (training) and Uncategorized (to predict)
    labeled = [
        {"operation": t.operation, "details": t.details, "category": t.category} 
        for t in all_tx if t.category != "Uncategorized"
    ]
    
    to_predict = [t for t in all_tx if t.category == "Uncategorized"]
    
    if not labeled or not to_predict:
        return {"message": "Not enough data to categorize"}

    # 3. Train Model
    service = CategorizationService()
    service.train(labeled)
    
    # 4. Predict
    prediction_data = [{"operation": t.operation, "details": t.details} for t in to_predict]
    results = service.predict_categories(prediction_data)
    
    # 5. Update Database
    count = 0
    for tx_obj, res in zip(to_predict, results):
        if res['category'] != "Uncategorized":
            tx_obj.category = res['category']
            count += 1
            
    db.commit()
    return {"message": f"Successfully categorized {count} transactions"}

import numpy as np
import datetime
import pandas as pd
from typing import Any

def sanitize_data(data: Any) -> Any:
    """
    Recursively sanitizes data to be JSON compliant.
    - Converts NaN/Inf to None (null)
    - Converts datetime/date/Timestamp to ISO strings
    """
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        return {k: sanitize_data(v) for k, v in data.items()}
    elif isinstance(data, list):
        return [sanitize_data(v) for v in data]
    elif isinstance(data, (datetime.datetime, datetime.date, pd.Timestamp)):
        return data.isoformat()
    elif isinstance(data, float):
        if np.isnan(data) or np.isinf(data):
            return None
        return data
    else:
        return data

def parse_salary_pdf(file_path: str) -> dict:

@app.post("/api/upload")

    files: List[UploadFile] = File(...),

    db: Session = Depends(get_db)
):
    os.makedirs("data/uploads", exist_ok=True)
    
    results = []
    total_imported = 0
    
    for file in files:
        file_path = f"data/uploads/{file.filename}"
        with open(file_path, "wb") as buffer:
            shutil.copyfileobj(file.file, buffer)
        
        logger.info(f"Received file {file.filename} for doc_type {doc_type}")
        
        try:
            if doc_type == "statement":
                actual_source = source
                if file.filename.endswith('.csv'):
                    actual_source = "csv"
                
                parser = ParserFactory.get_parser(actual_source)
                parsed_transactions = parser.parse(file_path)
                
                count = 0
                for t in parsed_transactions:
                    exists = db.query(Transaction).filter(
                        Transaction.date == t["date"],
                        Transaction.amount == t["amount"],
                        Transaction.operation == t["operation"],
                        Transaction.details == t["details"],
                        Transaction.account_id == t["account_id"]
                    ).first()
                    
                    if not exists:
                        db.add(Transaction(**t))
                        count += 1
                
                db.commit()
                total_imported += count
                results.append({"filename": file.filename, "status": "success", "rows": count})
                
            elif doc_type == "salary":
                extracted_data = parse_salary_pdf(file_path)
                salary_entry = Salary(
                    filename=file.filename,
                    **extracted_data
                )
                db.add(salary_entry)
                db.commit()
                results.append({"filename": file.filename, "status": "success"})
                
        except Exception as e:

            logger.error(f"Error processing file {file.filename}: {str(e)}")
            results.append({"filename": file.filename, "status": "error", "message": str(e)})

    return {
        "status": "completed",
        "type": doc_type,
        "results": results,
        "total_imported_rows": total_imported
    }

@app.get("/api/transactions")
async def get_transactions(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    txs = db.query(Transaction).order_by(Transaction.date.desc()).all()
    # Convert ORM objects to dicts manually to ensure sanitize_data can see all fields
    data = []
    for tx in txs:

        db.refresh(new_tx)

    if not db_tx:

    for key, value in transaction.items():

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer
from sklearn.naive_bayes import MultinomialNB
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from typing import List, Dict, Any

class CategorizationService:
    def __init__(self):
        self.pipeline = make_pipeline(
            CountVectorizer(),
            MultinomialNB()
        )
        self.is_trained = False

    def train(self, transactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]):
        """
        Trains the model using existing categorized transactions.
        transactions: List of dicts with 'details', 'operation', and 'category'.
        """
        df = pd.DataFrame(transactions)
        
        # Filter rows that have a valid category
        labeled_df = df[df['category'] != 'Uncategorized'].copy()
        
        if len(labeled_df) < 5:
            self.is_trained = False
            return # Not enough data to train

        # Create feature text: combine operation and details
        labeled_df['feature_text'] = labeled_df['operation'].astype(str) + " " + labeled_df['details'].astype(str)
        
        X = labeled_df['feature_text']
        y = labeled_df['category']

        self.pipeline.fit(X, y)
        self.is_trained = True

    def predict_categories(self, new_transactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Predicts categories for a list of new transactions.
        """
        if not self.is_trained:
            return new_transactions # Return as is if model isn't trained

        df = pd.DataFrame(new_transactions)
        if df.empty:
            return []

        df['feature_text'] = df['operation'].astype(str) + " " + df['details'].astype(str)
        
        # Predict
        predicted_categories = self.pipeline.predict(df['feature_text'])
        # Get probabilities to apply a confidence threshold
        probs = self.pipeline.predict_proba(df['feature_text'])
        
        confidence_threshold = 0.6
        
        final_categories = []
        for cat, prob in zip(predicted_categories, probs):
            if max(prob) >= confidence_threshold:
                final_categories.append(cat)
            else:
                final_categories.append("Uncategorized")
        
        # Update the list
        for i, tx in enumerate(new_transactions):
            tx['category'] = final_categories[i]
            
        return new_transactions

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from prophet import Prophet
from typing import List, Dict, Any
import datetime

class ForecastingService:
    def __init__(self, transactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]):
        self.df = pd.DataFrame(transactions)
        if not self.df.empty:
            self.df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(self.df['date'])

    def generate_forecast(self, days: int = 30) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if self.df.empty or len(self.df) < 5:
            return {"error": "Not enough data for forecasting"}

        daily_sum = self.df.groupby('date')['amount'].sum().reset_index()
        daily_sum = daily_sum.sort_values('date')
        daily_sum['balance'] = daily_sum['amount'].cumsum()

        prophet_df = daily_sum.rename(columns={'date': 'ds', 'balance': 'y'})

        model = Prophet(
            yearly_seasonality=True,
            weekly_seasonality=True,
            daily_seasonality=False,
            changepoint_prior_scale=0.05
        )
        model.fit(prophet_df)

        future = model.make_future_dataframe(periods=days)
        forecast = model.predict(future)

        # Standardize for JSON: Convert to dict and handle NaN
        result = forecast[['ds', 'yhat', 'yhat_lower', 'yhat_upper']].tail(days).copy()
        result['ds'] = result['ds'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        
        # Critical fix: replace NaN with None
        clean_result = result.replace({np.nan: None}).to_dict(orient='records')
        
        return {
            "forecast": clean_result,
            "current_balance": float(daily_sum['balance'].iloc[-1])
        }

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Dict, Any

class StatsService:
    def __init__(self, transactions: List[Dict[str, Any]]):
        self.df = pd.DataFrame(transactions)
        if not self.df.empty:
            self.df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(self.df['date'])
            # Sort by date to ensure cumulative balance is correct
            self.df = self.df.sort_values('date')

    def get_monthly_summary(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        if self.df.empty:
            return []

        # We need to calculate the running balance first
        self.df['running_balance'] = self.df['amount'].cumsum()

        self.df['month'] = self.df['date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m')
        
        # Group by month
        # For income/spend, we sum the monthly deltas
        # For balance, we take the LAST balance of that month
        summary = self.df.groupby('month').agg({
            'amount': [
                ('income', lambda x: round(float(x[x > 0].sum()), 2)),
                ('spend', lambda x: round(float(abs(x[x < 0].sum())), 2))
            ],
            'running_balance': [('balance', lambda x: round(float(x.iloc[-1]), 2))]
        }).reset_index()

        # Flatten multi-index columns
        summary.columns = ['month', 'income', 'spend', 'balance']
        
        summary = summary.sort_values('month')
        
        # Standardize for JSON
        return summary.replace({np.nan: None}).to_dict(orient='records')

    def get_category_breakdown(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        if self.df.empty:
            return []

        # Filter only expenses
        expenses = self.df[self.df['amount'] < 0]
        
        if expenses.empty:
            return []

        breakdown = expenses.groupby('category')['amount'].sum().abs().reset_index()
        breakdown['amount'] = breakdown['amount'].round(2)
        breakdown = breakdown.sort_values('amount', ascending=False)
        
        return breakdown.replace({np.nan: None}).to_dict(orient='records')

    def get_kpi(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        if self.df.empty:
            return {"total_balance": 0.0, "total_income": 0.0, "total_expense": 0.0}

        return {
            "total_balance": round(float(self.df['amount'].sum() or 0.0), 2),
            "total_income": round(float(self.df.loc[self.df['amount'] > 0, 'amount'].sum() or 0.0), 2),
            "total_expense": round(float(self.df.loc[self.df['amount'] < 0, 'amount'].sum() or 0.0), 2)
        }

        "Operazione": "operation",
        "Dettagli": "details",
        "Conto o carta": "account",

    }

    def parse_sanpaolo(file_path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Process Intesa San Paolo Excel file format."""
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            df = pd.read_excel(file_path)
        
        # Remove header rows (Intesa statements usually have meta info at the top)
        df = df[df.iloc[:, 0].notna()]
        
        # Set header from first valid row and remove it
        new_header = df.iloc[0]
        df = df[1:].rename(columns=new_header)
        
        # Reset index and rename columns to internal standard
        df = df.reset_index(drop=True)
        df = df.rename(columns=BankParser.COLUMN_MAPPINGS)
        
        # Ensure correct types
        df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])
        df["amount"] = df["amount"].apply(lambda x: float(Decimal(str(x)).quantize(Decimal("0.01"))))
        
        # Add internal tracking columns

        df["subcategory"] = "None"
        df["comment"] = ""
        
        return df

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import datetime
from typing import List, Dict, Any

class BaseBankParser(ABC):
    """
    Abstract Base Class for all bank statement parsers.
    Ensures that every module returns data in the Universal Financial Format.
    """
    
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def bank_name(self) -> str:
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def parse(self, file_path: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Parses the file and returns a list of dictionaries 
        matching the Transaction database model.
        """
        pass

    def standardize_dataframe(self, df: pd.DataFrame, mapping: Dict[str, str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Helper to rename columns and ensure UFF (Universal Financial Format)."""
        return df.rename(columns=mapping)

    def sanitize_for_json(self, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Recursively converts dates, timestamps and NaNs into JSON-serializable formats.
        """
        sanitized = {}
        for key, value in data.items():
            # Check for various date/time types using the datetime module safely
            if isinstance(value, (datetime.datetime, datetime.date, pd.Timestamp)):
                sanitized[key] = value.isoformat()
            elif isinstance(value, float) and (np.isnan(value) or np.isinf(value)):
                sanitized[key] = None
            elif isinstance(value, dict):
                sanitized[key] = self.sanitize_for_json(value)
            elif isinstance(value, list):
                sanitized[key] = [
                    self.sanitize_for_json(v) if isinstance(v, dict) else v 
                    for v in value
                ]
            else:
                sanitized[key] = value
        return sanitized
